title: Eighth Amendment and State Religion
subtitle: On 7 June 1988, Bangladesh’s parliament passed the Constitution (Eighth Amendment) Act
summary: On 7 June 1988, Bangladesh’s parliament passed the Constitution (Eighth Amendment) Act. It inserted Article 2A declaring Islam the state religion while allowing other religions to be practised in peace and harmony; it also created six permanent High Court Division benches outside Dhaka.

claimCitations.claim: On 7 June 1988, Bangladesh’s parliament passed the Constitution (Eighth Amendment) Act. It inserted Article 2A declaring Islam the state religion while allowing other religions to be practised in peace and harmony; it also created six permanent High Court Division benches outside Dhaka.

The amendment placed a state-religion clause in the Constitution and became a focus of debate over religious identity and secular constitutional principles. The Supreme Court later struck down the separate High Court bench provision; that ruling did not concern Article 2A.
Article 2A remains in the constitutional framework alongside guarantees concerning other religions; debate over state religion and secular principles continues.
